concepts.title: Nutrition in Animals
concepts.definition: Food's journey runs mouth to anus: chewed by teeth, moistened by saliva, pushed down the foodpipe, churned in the stomach, digested by intestinal juices, and absorbed by the small intestine's tiny finger-like villi.
concepts.formula: digestion = ingestion + digestion + absorption + assimilation + egestion
concepts.key_idea: Digestion breaks food into molecules small enough to pass into blood: each organ plays its part on the assembly line.

concepts.title: Respiration in Animals
concepts.definition: Every animal releases energy from food by respiration: lungs draw in oxygen and give out carbon dioxide in land animals, gills filter dissolved oxygen in fish, and skin helps in earthworms and frogs.
concepts.formula: food + oxygen = energy + carbon dioxide + water
concepts.key_idea: Respiration is combustion under control: oxygen burns food gently to release usable energy.

concepts.title: Breathing Mechanism and the Lungs
concepts.definition: Breathing runs on pressure: the diaphragm flattens and ribs rise to draw air in, then relax to push air out; the balloon-in-bottle model of the chapter shows the lungs inflating and deflating with each stroke.
concepts.key_idea: Breathing is pumping by pressure: chest space grows, air rushes in; chest space shrinks, air leaves.

concepts.title: Excretion and Circulation
concepts.definition: Blood carries digested food and oxygen to every cell and returns with wastes; the kidneys filter this blood, removing urea and extra water as urine, keeping the body's inner sea clean and steady.
concepts.key_idea: Transport and cleaning run together: circulation delivers, kidneys discard, and the body stays fit inside.
